quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Your scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.
Checking your rearview mirror often.
Not using the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly as part of your normal scanning routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause your motorcycle to skid.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slow or stopped:

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slowly moving vehicles is dangerous. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out of windows. Even though motorcycles are small, they need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means that they see you.
Does not mean they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will properly yield to you. A driver can look directly at a motorcyclist and still fail to see them.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see farther down the road.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being struck from behind.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles. Visibility is lower at night and you need extra time and space to react to hazards ahead.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders may cause you to steer the wrong way.

questions.question: A person under age 21 will receive a DUI for riding with a minimum blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.02 percent.
0.04 percent.
0.08 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.02 percent.
questions.explanation: For people under age 21, a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.02 percent or higher is a DUI conviction.

questions.question: Eye protection is:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Not required, but recommended.
Only required for inexperienced motorcycle users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection while on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: Before starting out, you should make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Before you ride, make sure your fuel supply valve is open. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines from before, but it will stall once those lines empty.

questions.question: If wearing a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool while in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.
questions.explanation: A sturdy riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. In hot weather, jackets also help prevent dehydration. Many riding jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake gives about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Always use both brakes when you stop.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road marks:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks where the traffic lane ends on the right side.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, they should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: When riding over textured pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down at the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: When riding over textured pavement in a work zone, keep your head and eyes up. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and don't fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcycle rider should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Prepare the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, choose a lane position that other drivers can see you in. Get your clutch and brakes ready to react fast. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Do not make sudden speed or position changes, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass. A dashed line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do these actions separately. Never brake while swerving because your motorcycle can fall over.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
It is usually hard for the driver to see you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in a position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, this means the center of the lane. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and do not brake.
Shift your weight to the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake only on the good wheel and pull off the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and do not brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and stay on a straight path. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down significantly before leaving the road.

questions.question: When riding in a group, less experienced riders should be:

options.text: In the front.
Just behind the lead rider.
In the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.
